prompt: Write a command to list all modules currently loaded in your PowerShell session.
hints: Without any extra parameters, Get-Module shows loaded modules.
You do not need -ListAvailable for currently loaded modules.

validation.hintOnFail: Do not use -ListAvailable — that shows all installed modules, not just loaded ones.

explanation: Get-Module without parameters lists only the modules currently loaded in the session. Add -ListAvailable to see all installed modules.

prompt: Write a command to search the PowerShell Gallery for modules with names containing 'SharePoint'.
hints: Use Find-Module to search the online gallery.
Use the -Name parameter with a wildcard pattern.
Wildcards in PowerShell use the * character.

validation.hintOnFail: Use Find-Module to search the PowerShell Gallery.
Search for modules containing 'SharePoint' (use wildcards like *SharePoint*).

explanation: Find-Module searches the PowerShell Gallery (PSGallery) for modules matching the pattern. Wildcards let you find modules even when you don't know the exact name.

prompt: Write a command to install the 'PnP.PowerShell' module for the current user only (without requiring admin privileges).
hints: Add -Scope CurrentUser to install without admin rights.

validation.hintOnFail: Specify the module name as PnP.PowerShell.
Add -Scope CurrentUser to install without administrator privileges.

explanation: Install-Module downloads the module from the PowerShell Gallery and installs it. -Scope CurrentUser places it in your personal module directory, so no admin elevation is needed.

prompt: Write a command to explicitly import the 'Microsoft.Graph' module into your current session.
hints: Use Import-Module to load a module.
This forces the module to load even if it hasn't been auto-imported yet.

validation.hintOnFail: Specify Microsoft.Graph as the module name.

explanation: Import-Module explicitly loads a module and all its commands into the current session. This is useful at the top of scripts to ensure dependencies are available.

prompt: Write a command to show all installed versions of the 'Az' module on your system, displaying the Name and Version properties.
hints: Use Get-Module with -ListAvailable to see installed modules.
Specify -Name Az to filter to just that module.
Pipe to Select-Object to pick the Name and Version properties.

validation.hintOnFail: Use Get-Module to find installed modules.
Add -ListAvailable to see all installed modules, not just loaded ones.
Filter by module name Az using the -Name parameter.
Pipe to Select-Object to display specific properties.
Use the pipeline | to connect Get-Module to Select-Object.
Include the Name property in Select-Object.
Include the Version property in Select-Object.

explanation: Get-Module -ListAvailable shows all installed versions of a module. Piping to Select-Object Name, Version gives a clean summary of what is available on your system.
